privacyPage.title: Purpleship Privacy Policy
privacyPage.subtitle: Privacy policy regarding the collection, use, and management of personal information for Purpleship services.

section1.title: 1. Scope and Basic Principles
section1.p1: This policy applies to Purpleship (hereinafter "Company") and all services operated by the Company (e.g., Stampit, Movit, Qnote, WorldCanvas, etc.).
section1.p2: The Company collects only the minimum personal information necessary to provide services. Additional requirements specific to each service are separately stated in the "Service-Specific Notices" section.

section2.title: 2. Information Collected and Purpose of Use (General)
section2.intro: The Company collects only the minimum information necessary for service provision and customer support.
section2.li1: Website usage: Access logs, browser/OS information, service usage history through cookies and similar technologies (for statistics and service improvement)
section2.li2: Customer inquiry processing: Name, email, and inquiry content received through inquiry channels (email, etc.)
section2.li3: Technical logs: Error logs, device information (model, OS version, etc.) for stability analysis

analytics.title: 2.1 Web/App Analytics Tools
analytics.p1: We may collect anonymized usage statistics using analytics tools such as Google Analytics. We apply IP anonymization and pseudonymization and do not directly identify individuals.

section3.title: 3. Retention and Use Period of Personal Information
section3.li1: Data is retained only for the minimum period required by law or internal policy and is promptly destroyed thereafter.
section3.li2: Access logs: Retained for 3 months in accordance with the Communications Privacy Protection Act and then automatically destroyed.
section3.li3: Customer inquiry records: Retained for 3 years after resolution for dispute preparation and then destroyed.
section3.li4: Account and service data: Deleted without delay upon purpose fulfillment or account termination.

section4.title: 4. Third-Party Provision and International Transfer
section4.p1: In principle, the Company does not provide users' personal information to third parties. However, it may be provided exceptionally in the following cases:
section4.li1: When the user has given explicit prior consent
section4.li2: When there is a legal basis or a lawful request from investigative authorities
section4.p2: Information transfers by the external map and advertising services used by Movit on iOS, and by the optional Google Drive backup, are described separately in “Additional notice for Movit on iOS” below.
section4.p3: Overseas transfers to Google LLC (United States) through the RoboEscape app's ad SDK are described in the ‘RoboEscape’ section below.
section4.p4: Overseas transfers to Google LLC (United States) through the Movit app's ad SDK (iOS and Android) are described in the ‘Movit’ section below.
section4.p5: Overseas transfers to Google LLC (United States) through the Squadron Rush app's ad SDK (iOS and Android) are described in the ‘Squadron Rush’ section below.

section5.title: 5. Outsourcing of Personal Information Processing
section5.p1: We may outsource work to external parties to maintain service quality, and we impose security, re-outsourcing restrictions, and management/supervision obligations on contractors.
section5.li1: Service usage analysis: Google LLC (Google Analytics)
section5.li2: User-selected backup/sync: Apple iCloud Drive, Google Drive, etc.
section5.li3: Ad serving, ad measurement and fraud prevention (RoboEscape, Movit, Squadron Rush): Google LLC (Google AdMob)

section6.title: 6. User Rights and How to Exercise Them
section6.p1: Users may exercise the following rights at any time, and the Company will take action without delay.
section6.li1: Withdrawal of consent: You can change or withdraw permissions such as location and notifications through service or device settings at any time.
section6.li2: Request for access, correction, deletion, or suspension: You can request from the Company or manage directly through provided screens/settings.
section6.li3: Filing for remedy through personal information protection centers, dispute resolution committees, etc.

section7.title: 7. Security Measures
section7.p1: The Company takes the following measures to ensure the safety of personal information:
section7.li1: Minimizing access rights and managing access records
section7.li2: Encryption and key management for transmission and storage
section7.li3: Regular security patches and vulnerability checks
section7.li4: Training and inspection for personal information handlers

section8.title: 8. Service-Specific Notices
section8.intro: The following provides additional personal information processing details specific to each service.

stampit.title: Stampit (Membership Management)
stampit.summary: An app for managing membership and coupon usage. Data is stored locally on the device by default.
stampit.li1: Information collected: Store/membership name, stamp/visit records, notification settings
stampit.li2: Storage location: Stored locally on the user's device and not transmitted to Company servers.
stampit.li3: Backup/Sync: If selected by the user, backed up in file format to personal iCloud/Google Drive.

movit.title: Movit (Movement Records)
movit.summary: Manages movement records and favorites. Default storage location is the user's device.
movit.li1: Access, collection, and use: When you enable route recording, Movit accesses and collects precise location data on your device, including while the app is closed or not in use, to create movement routes and exploration records.
movit.li2: Storage and server collection: Location data is stored only on the user's device. We do not transmit location data to or collect it on Company servers.
movit.li3: Optional permissions: Location (including background) and notification permissions may be used for route logging and alerts; collection stops when you disable them.
movit.li4: Backup/Sync: Location data is backed up to your personal cloud (e.g., Google Drive) only when you explicitly request it.
movit.li5: When third-party map/location SDKs are used for maps or navigation, the provider’s privacy policy also applies.

ios.title: Additional notice for Movit on iOS
ios.locationP1: When you allow location access, Movit stores your movement records on your device. On iOS the app requests “While Using the App” location permission; while recording, it uses background location updates and the system location indicator. You can stop recording from the app menu or withdraw location permission in iOS Settings. Movement records are not uploaded to Purpleship servers. If you choose a Google Drive backup, the backup file is sent to your own Google Drive account.
ios.mapP1: Movit displays the map with map tiles fetched from MapTiler’s servers. For this, the tile coordinates and zoom level of the map area being displayed, your IP address and an app identification string are sent to MapTiler. The purpose is to deliver the requested map images. The app does not upload your stored movement record files to MapTiler. The displayed map area may correspond to your current location. MapTiler’s privacy policy is available at https://www.maptiler.com/privacy-policy/.
ios.adsP1: Movit uses Google AdMob banner ads, optional rewarded ads and the Google User Messaging Platform (UMP). Ad requests are sent to Google. The ad SDK processing items published by Google are: IP address and the approximate location derived from it, app- or developer-scoped device identifiers, ad impression, video view and interaction information, and error and performance information. The purposes are third-party ad delivery, measurement and analytics, and diagnosis and improvement of the ad SDK. Processing of each item depends on device permissions, consent status and Google’s ad processing. The app does not put GPS coordinates or stored movement records directly into ad requests.
ios.adsP2: The app updates consent information through UMP, shows any required form, and requests ads only once ad requests are allowed. If UMP requires a privacy options entry point, you can reopen it from the app menu. Purpleship does not use this advertising data for its own marketing or to promote other apps. Google’s data processing is governed by the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).
ios.transfer: The recipient is Google LLC (United States; privacy inquiries: https://support.google.com/policies/contact/general_privacy_form). Items transferred: the ad SDK data listed above (IP address and the approximate location derived from it, app- or developer-scoped device identifiers, ad impressions, video views and interactions, and error and performance data), plus the advertising identifier (IDFA) if you allow tracking. Purposes: serving, measuring and analysing ads, and diagnosing and improving the ad SDK. The data is sent over the network when ads are requested while the app is in use, and is retained under Google's policies (https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention). The Company makes this transfer by disclosing these matters in this policy (Article 28-8(1)3 of the Personal Information Protection Act).
ios.refuse: How to refuse, and the effect: (1) Choose ‘Ask App Not to Track’ when the app first asks, or turn off tracking for Movit in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking. The advertising identifier (IDFA) is then not shared and personalized ads are limited. However, some data, such as the IP address and diagnostic data, is still sent when ads are requested; the app stays usable. (2) If you uninstall the app, all transfers stop.

stats.title: Movit app usage statistics (Android and iOS)
stats.p1: To understand how each version is used, Movit sends once per day on days the app is opened: a random install identifier created on first launch (not generated from device or account information), the app version, the operating system and platform (Android/iOS), and a data-format version, to Purpleship's statistics server. Movement records, GPS location coordinates, advertising identifiers and account information are not sent.
stats.p2: The statistics server does not store the IP address. Together with the daily record for each install identifier, it stores the country code determined from the connecting IP address and a device type derived from the app's fixed identification string. The statistics server runs on Cloudflare infrastructure.
stats.p3: The install identifier is removed from the device when the app is deleted or its data is cleared. Daily records on the server are kept while the statistics purpose continues and are deleted without delay once the purpose is achieved, such as when the service ends.

android.ads: Ads (Android): The Android app includes the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob) and Google User Messaging Platform (UMP) and shows ads.
android.transfer: Overseas transfer (ads, Android): The recipient is Google LLC (United States; privacy inquiries: https://support.google.com/policies/contact/general_privacy_form). Items transferred: device identifiers such as the advertising ID and app set ID; IP address (which may be used to estimate approximate location); ad interaction data; and diagnostic data for the app and the ad SDK. Purposes: serving ads, analytics (including ad measurement), and fraud prevention. The data is sent over the network when ads are requested while the app is in use, and is retained under Google's policies (https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention). The Company makes this transfer by disclosing these matters in this policy (Article 28-8(1)3 of the Personal Information Protection Act). Source: Google, Google Mobile Ads SDK (Legacy) data disclosure (https://developers.google.com/admob/android/privacy/play-data-disclosure).
android.refuse: How to refuse, and the effect (Android): (1) If you reset or delete the advertising ID in the device settings, personalized ads are limited. However, some data, such as the IP address and diagnostic data, is still sent when ads are requested; the app stays usable. (2) If you uninstall the app, all transfers stop.

qnote.title: Qnote (Notes/Checklists)
qnote.summary: Note/checklist data is stored locally on the device by default.
qnote.li1: Information collected: Notes, checklists, tags, attachments created by the user
qnote.li2: Storage location: Stored locally on the device and not transmitted to Company servers.
qnote.li3: Backup/Sync: If selected by the user, saved to personal cloud or exported as files.

roboescape.title: RoboEscape (Stealth Escape Game)
roboescape.summary: A robot prison-break stealth game. Game progress and purchase-confirmation data are stored only on the device and are not sent to Purpleship servers. The app includes Google AdMob ads (interstitial and rewarded) and Google Play billing.
roboescape.ads: Ads: An interstitial ad may appear when you move on from the stage-clear screen, and rewarded ads play only when you choose to watch them. Buying Remove Ads or the Starter Pack turns off interstitial ads. A maximum ad content rating of G is planned.
roboescape.iap: In-app purchases: Remove Ads and the Starter Pack (Remove Ads + an exclusive color palette) are sold through Google Play billing (Play Billing). Google collects payment-method information directly; the Company does not receive it. To confirm purchases, the app stores only the product ID, the time granted and a hash of the purchase token on the device.
roboescape.transfer: Overseas transfer (ads): The recipient is Google LLC (United States; privacy inquiries: https://support.google.com/policies/contact/general_privacy_form). Items transferred: device identifiers such as the advertising ID and app set ID, and device information (including mobile network type and carrier information); IP address (which may be used to estimate approximate location); ad interaction data (app launches, taps, ad views); and diagnostic data for the app and the ad SDK. Purposes: serving ads, analytics (including ad measurement), and fraud prevention. The data is sent over the network (TLS-encrypted) while the app is in use and is retained under Google's policies (https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention). The Company makes this transfer by disclosing these matters in this policy (Article 28-8(1)3 of the Personal Information Protection Act).
roboescape.refuse: How to refuse, and the effect: There are two ways. (1) If you reset or delete the advertising ID in the device settings, personalized ads are limited. However, some data, such as the IP address, device information and diagnostic data, is still sent when ads are requested. After deletion the app receives a string of zeros instead of the ID, and the game stays playable. (2) If you uninstall the app, all transfers stop.
roboescape.consent: Consent management: The app uses Google User Messaging Platform (UMP) to check whether consent is required and shows a consent form only where it is (for example, in the EEA). If you decline, the app does not request ads.
roboescape.sources: Sources: Google, GMA Next-Gen SDK data disclosure (https://developers.google.com/admob/android/next-gen/privacy/play-data-disclosure); How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services (https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites); Google Play, Advertising ID (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6048248). Google processes the data under the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).
roboescape.age: Audience: The app is intended for users aged 16 and over and is not directed at children. The Company does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 14. If it learns that such information has been processed, it will promptly destroy any it holds (such as inquiry emails) and explain how to delete data left on the device or with Google.
roboescape.permissions: Permissions and SDKs: internet, network state, advertising ID (AD_ID), basic phone state (READ_BASIC_PHONE_STATE), Google Play billing (BILLING), keep awake (WAKE_LOCK), foreground service, and an app-internal receiver-protection permission. READ_BASIC_PHONE_STATE is a normal (non-dangerous) permission declared by Google's ad SDK. Google's ad SDK may read the mobile network type and carrier information to serve ads; neither the app nor the SDK reads phone numbers or call content or call state. This information is part of the ‘device information’ in the overseas transfer above. There are no location, contacts, camera or microphone permissions. SDKs: Google Mobile Ads (GMA Next-Gen) 1.4.0, Google UMP 4.0.0 and Google Play Billing 9.1.0; there are no analytics or crash-reporting SDKs.
roboescape.retention: Retention: Game progress, settings and purchase-confirmation data stay only on the device and are deleted with the app (Android auto-backup is off). Inquiry emails are kept for 3 years as records of consumer complaints or dispute handling, then destroyed (Enforcement Decree of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, Article 6(1)4). Payment and order records are kept by Google Play.
roboescape.analytics: Analytics: The site analytics in 2.1, such as Google Analytics, apply to the website, not to the RoboEscape app. The app's play log stays on the device and is not sent.
roboescape.inAppLink: In-app notice: A link to this policy will be added to the app's settings screen.

squadronrush.title: Squadron Rush (Shooting Game)
squadronrush.summary: A vertical shooting game. There is no account or login. Game progress is stored only on the device and is not sent to Purpleship servers. The app includes Google AdMob ads (banner, interstitial and rewarded) and in-app purchases (Google Play billing on Android, Apple App Store in-app purchase on iOS).
squadronrush.ads: Ads: The app shows Google AdMob ads through the Google Mobile Ads Unity plugin. Banner ads appear on the menu, stage select, shop and result screens, and not during gameplay or on the pause or settings screens. An interstitial ad may appear when you leave a stage result screen, and rewarded ads play only when you choose to watch them (to revive after failing, or to double the coin reward). Buying Remove Ads (remove_ads) or the Starter Pack (starter_pack) turns off banner and interstitial ads; rewarded ads remain optional. The app sets the maximum ad content rating to G. The app does not add a separate ‘non-personalized ads’ flag to ad requests; whether ads are personalized depends on your UMP consent choice, the device's advertising-ID settings and Google's policies. On iOS the app does not show Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt, so the advertising identifier (IDFA) is not provided to Google; the Google ad SDK uses Apple's SKAdNetwork for ad attribution.
squadronrush.iap: In-app purchases: Remove Ads (remove_ads) and the Starter Pack (starter_pack; Remove Ads + two starter skins) are sold through Unity IAP, using Google Play billing (Play Billing) on Android and Apple App Store in-app purchase on iOS. Both are non-consumable and can be restored. Google or Apple collects payment-method information directly; the Company does not receive it. The app's save file stores only whether each product is owned (true/false), and a store restore overwrites these flags. Payment and order records are kept by Google Play or Apple.
squadronrush.transfer: Overseas transfer (ads): The recipient is Google LLC (United States; privacy inquiries: https://support.google.com/policies/contact/general_privacy_form). Items transferred on Android: device identifiers such as the advertising ID and app set ID; device information; IP address (which may be used to estimate approximate location); ad interaction data; and diagnostic data for the app and the ad SDK. Purposes: serving ads, analytics (including ad measurement), and fraud prevention. The data is sent over the network when ads are requested while the app is in use, and is retained under Google's policies (https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention). The Company makes this transfer by disclosing these matters in this policy (Article 28-8(1)3 of the Personal Information Protection Act).
squadronrush.transferIos: Overseas transfer (ads, iOS): On iOS the recipient, purposes, timing, retention and basis are the same as above. The items are the same kinds of data as on Android (device information, IP address, ad interaction data, and diagnostic data for the app and the ad SDK), but the advertising identifier (IDFA) is not provided, because the app does not show the ATT prompt; app- or developer-scoped identifiers may be used.
squadronrush.refuse: How to refuse, and the effect: (1) On Android, if you reset or delete the advertising ID in the device settings, personalized ads are limited. However, some data, such as the IP address, device information and diagnostic data, is still sent when ads are requested; the game stays playable. Where UMP consent applies, you can decline, or change your choices with the privacy options button on the settings screen. (2) If you uninstall the app, all transfers stop. Buying ad removal stops banner and interstitial ad requests (rewarded ads only if you choose them).
squadronrush.consent: Consent management: The app uses Google User Messaging Platform (UMP) to check whether consent is required and shows a consent form only where it is (for example, in the EEA or the UK). Ads are requested only once UMP allows ad requests. When UMP requires a privacy options entry point, the settings screen shows a button to reopen it. Players who have bought ad removal are not shown the consent form.
squadronrush.sources: Sources: Google, Google Mobile Ads SDK data disclosure (https://developers.google.com/admob/android/privacy/play-data-disclosure); How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services (https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites); Google Play, Advertising ID (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6048248). Google processes the data under the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).
squadronrush.age: Audience: The game is for a general audience and is not directed at children (maximum ad content rating: G). The Company does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 14. If it learns that such information has been processed, it will promptly destroy any it holds (such as inquiry emails) and explain how to delete data left on the device or with Google.
squadronrush.permissions: Permissions and SDKs: On Android the app uses internet (INTERNET), network state (ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE), advertising ID (AD_ID), the Android Privacy Sandbox ad permissions declared by Google's ad SDK (ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION, ACCESS_ADSERVICES_TOPICS), Google Play billing (BILLING), keep awake (WAKE_LOCK), foreground service (FOREGROUND_SERVICE), and an app-internal receiver-protection permission. There are no location, contacts, camera, microphone or phone permissions; on iOS the app makes no camera, location, microphone or tracking permission requests. SDKs: Google Mobile Ads Unity plugin 11.6.0 (Android Google Mobile Ads SDK 25.5.0), Google UMP 4.0.0 and Unity IAP 5.5.0. There are no analytics or crash-reporting SDKs; Unity Analytics, crash reporting and performance reporting are turned off in the project.
squadronrush.retention: Retention: Save data (stage progress and stars, coins, best endless score, owned and equipped skins, purchase flags and sound settings) is kept in the app's storage on the device and is deleted with the app. Android's automatic backup is not turned off in this app, so depending on your device settings the save file may be included in your own Google account backup (managed by Google, not sent to Purpleship). Inquiry emails are kept for 3 years as records of consumer complaints or dispute handling, then destroyed (Enforcement Decree of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, Article 6(1)4). Payment and order records are kept by Google Play or Apple.
squadronrush.analytics: Analytics: The site analytics in 2.1, such as Google Analytics, apply to the website, not to the Squadron Rush app. The app has no analytics service connected and sends no play data.
squadronrush.inAppLink: In-app notice: The app's settings screen links to this section (https://purpleship.io/privacy/#squadronrush). Inquiries can be sent to the contact in section 9 (captain@purpleship.io).

worldcanvasTermsPage.title: WorldCanvas Purchase Terms
worldcanvasTermsPage.subtitle: This section sets forth additional terms for purchasing and using paid products and virtual currency (Purple) in WorldCanvas.

section1.title: 1. Definitions
section1.d1: "Paid Products" means digital content, permissions, or virtual currency provided through payment.
section1.d2: "Purple" refers to virtual currency (points/credits) usable within WorldCanvas services, which cannot be exchanged for cash.
section1.d3: "Consumption" means using Purple to purchase functions/items or increase usage limits.

section2.title: 2. Purple Usage
section2.p1: Users can purchase Purple to use features within WorldCanvas. Specific uses are displayed in the service interface.
section2.li2: Example: Increasing the "pixel placement limit" for bulk pixel placement
section2.li3: Example: Other paid items/features (may be added in the future)

section3.title: 3. Payment and Delivery
section3.p1: Prices, contents, payment methods, and billing times are shown during the purchase process. Purple or permissions are provided immediately (or within a reasonable time) after payment.
section3.li1: Payments may be processed through third-party payment service providers.
section3.li2: Purchase history and payment details can be verified in the service or payment receipt.
section3.li3: For detailed pricing information, please refer to the pricing page.

section4.title: 4. Withdrawal (Refunds) and Exceptions
section4.p1: Digital content/virtual currency may be available for use immediately upon provision, and withdrawal may be restricted within the scope permitted by law. However, refunds or compensation may be provided in the following cases:
section4.li1: Cases where there is a company fault (non-delivery, incorrect delivery, etc.)
section4.li2: Cases with legitimate reasons (payment errors, duplicate payments, etc.)
section4.li4: If Purple has already been consumed, processing may exclude the consumed portion (within the scope not restricted by law).
section4.li5: For detailed refund policies, please refer to the refund policy page.

section5.title: 5. Minor Payments
section5.p1: Minors making payments may require legal guardian consent, and cancellation (refund) requests may be possible according to law.

section6.title: 6. Usage Restrictions and Recovery
section6.p1: If fraudulent payments, hacking/abuse, or terms violations are confirmed, we may recover granted Purple/permissions or restrict account usage according to applicable laws and service policies.

worldcanvasRefundPage.title: WorldCanvas Refund Policy
worldcanvasRefundPage.subtitle: Refund information for Paddle payment system

section1.title: 1. Payment Processing
section1.p1: All payments for WorldCanvas are processed by Paddle.com as the Merchant of Record. Paddle is an authorized payment service provider that handles payments, tax processing, and refunds.
section1.p2: Paddle's payment terms apply to purchases, and receipts and payment inquiries are processed through Paddle.

section2.title: 2. 14-Day Refund Guarantee
section2.highlight: You can request a refund within 14 days from the date of purchase without giving any reason.
section2.p1: The refund period expires 14 days after the payment completion date. To meet the cancellation deadline, it is sufficient to send your refund request before the 14-day period expires.
section2.p2: This refund guarantee is for consumer rights protection and applies to initial purchases.

section3.title: 3. How to Request a Refund
section3.intro: To request a refund, please use one of the following methods:
section3.li1: Paddle Customer Support: Request a refund directly at paddle.net
section3.li2: Email: Contact captain@purpleship.io with your purchase details (receipt/payment info)
section3.p1: For immediate processing, please provide the email address used for purchase and payment information when requesting a refund.

section4.title: 4. Refund Restrictions After 14 Days
section4.li1: After the 14-day period, if virtual currency (Purple) has already been used, refunds may be processed excluding the used portion.
section4.li2: Refund processing time may vary by payment method. (Card payments: up to 120 days, PayPal: up to 179 days)
section4.li3: Refunds may be denied in cases of fraudulent payments, abuse, or terms violations.
